answer: Each identity's usable standing is released only after a sequential, non-transferable custody period, and the release rate is super-linear in how many identities an operator runs, so a fleet cannot mature faster than one identity at a time. The cost of one more head is paid in full and is never amortised across the fleet. The ferrous is the serial tenure, the wharf the custody window that must elapse, and the umber the standing released at the end of it; the ferrous is personal, the wharf is not skippable, and the umber cannot be inherited by a sibling.
